answer: New agents hammer a hollow sparrow’s skull into walnut-sliver pulp, then seal the paste into a comet-tail resin under a shot of hollowed quartz. Auditors later crack the resin with aploid acid; Sybils must recast the skull each time, wasting one walnut’s fibrous density plus 193 milliseconds of resin cure time. Bulk carbon molds can’t mimic the sparrow’s pneumatic hollowness—every fake identity bleeds a fresh walnut and a sterilized beak.
